chunks: So far we have mentioned some reports and traditions, which prove the Imamate of the son of Imam Hasan Askari (a.s), his holy existence and occultation. These reports mention unseen matters and prophesize future events in an extraordinary manner, such that no one had any knowledge about them, except that Allah, the Mighty and the High may have bestowed him through the knowledge of His Prophet and these reports reached him through one whose veracity was testified beyond any doubt. Like for example, Husain bin Rauh. If his veracity had not been there, he would not have been as such [that he would not have had knowledge of unseen], because these miracles are never possible through liars. The conclusion is that when the veracity of the deputies of Imam (a.s) is proved, it also proves the existence of one through whom they are getting these blessings. However, we have not quoted everything recorded in this regard lest the book becomes lengthy, though it is mentioned in other books.
ai.seo_question: How do reports of the unseen prove the existence and Imamate of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi grounds the proof of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari’s (a.s.) occultation in the concept of *kharq al-‘ada* (miraculous exception to habit), arguing that knowledge of the unseen (*al-ghayb*) is exclusively divinely granted to the Prophet or his truthful deputies. He establishes a logical chain where the veracity of these deputies, confirmed by miracles not appearing on the tongues of liars, necessitates the actual existence of the Imam to whom the reports are attributed. While this excerpt serves as a concise epistemological justification, the full corpus of these reports is preserved in broader hadith collections to avoid redundancy in this specific text.
